items.body: Raveiac, a new rave-punk project from Turkey, released the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1” on SoundCloud on 2 October 2026. The five-track set gathers “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” tagged as techno on the platform. The compilation is part of a wider opening catalog. Raveiac released five tracks on 2 October: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It.” Two more, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit,” followed on 3 October, and “Backstall” closed the run on 4 October, for eight tracks in three days. There is no Bandcamp page yet. The catalog streams exclusively through Raveiac’s SoundCloud profile. Raveiac’s own description connects the project to “industrial rave, hard techno, breakbeat, EBM, gabber and digital hardcore,” through what it calls “a direct punk vocabulary: repeated commands, physical hooks and lyrics shaped by concrete rooms, surveillance, machinery, appetite and loss of control.” The project’s SoundCloud bio reads in full: “Rave-punk from Turkey. Dirty industrial raves, broken breaks, and digital decay. Repost what hits. Push it deeper underground.” ‘Rust & Strobe’ and ‘Swallow the Noise’ Raveiac singled out two tracks from the set for press attention. “Rust & Strobe” opens on metallic percussion and broken drums and closes on what the project calls “an acid-charged chorus.” “Swallow the Noise” is described as a faster industrial-rave track carried by a chanted vocal line and distorted production. Raveiac also presents a visual identity drawn from photocopied zines, neon imagery, torn paper, halftone noise and analog damage. About Raveiac Raveiac launched in October 2026 as an independent rave-punk project from Turkey. Between 2 and 4 October 2026, the project released eight tracks on SoundCloud: “Concrete Fever,” “Bite the Wire,” “Just One More,” “Swallow the Noise” and “I Feed It” on 2 October, “Rust & Strobe” and “Sweat & Slit” on 3 October, and “Backstall” on 4 October. Five of those tracks, “Backstall,” “Sweat & Slit,” “Rust & Strobe,” “Concrete Fever” and “Swallow the Noise,” make up the compilation “Rave-Punk Rituals Vol. 1”.

items.album: [2View] Drift :: Manic EP / Radius Etc :: Alive & Thriving EP (The Consumers Research and Development Label)
items.excerpt: The Consumers Research and Development Label is clearly not trying to be one thing, and that’s the most encouraging part of this reintroduction. A techno veteran finally putting out his own record after twenty years of platforming everyone else, sitting right next to a hip-hop travelogue built out of literal years of instability and constant movement, that’s a genuinely odd pairing on paper, and it works precisely because neither release is compromising to fit next to the other. &nbs
items.body: The Consumers Research and Development Label is clearly not trying to be one thing, and that’s the most encouraging part of this reintroduction. A techno veteran finally putting out his own record after twenty years of platforming everyone else, sitting right next to a hip-hop travelogue built out of literal years of instability and constant movement, that’s a genuinely odd pairing on paper, and it works precisely because neither release is compromising to fit next to the other.   Consumers finds its second wind Manic by Drift   Alive & Thriving by Radius Etc   There’s a good story behind why this review exists at all. The Consumers Research and Development Label ran independently through the 2000s before becoming an imprint of Someoddpilot Records, the Chicago label-turned-agency that also handled branding for Pitchfork back when that meant something specific in the industry, and later built brand identity work for clients like Drag City, Jagjaguwar, and Secretly Canadian. Geoffrey Wilson bought Consumers in 2023 with help from Chris Eichenseer, who founded Someoddpilot in 1999 and who Wilson had shared an office with from 2003 to 2008, before the label originally shut down. Somewhere in the years between closing and reopening, a flood destroyed the entire back stock. Whatever’s floating around on Discogs or eBay now is all that survived physically; the rest is gone. The label came back properly in November 2024 with a showcase at Public Works in Wicker Park, quiet after that, and this is its real reintroduction to a wider audience: two EPs, two very different sounds, one label figuring out what it wants to be the second time around. Drift’s Manic comes first and it’s a strange kind of debut for someone who’s clearly not new to any of this. Sean Krainik has run Parotic Records, the Midwest techno label, for over two decades, putting out records from DJ Slip, Johannes Heil, Matt Paffel, Dave Olson, and Mr. Projectile among others. He never released his own music on vinyl until now. Manic pulls from more than twenty years of writing tracks in the background while other people’s records took priority, and that accumulated time shows in how confidently unshowy this record is. This leans techno and IDM more than anything experimental, dancefloor-facing and beat-heavy across the whole tracklist. The title track builds itself up layer by layer into a pulsating beat while TV dialogue keeps pulling focus sideways, a small disruption that never fully resolves. Nothing here is trying to be difficult, and nothing here needed to be. “R$W” and “Osmosis” are the two that stick hardest. Different rhythms, same underlying intent—Krainik chasing something gritty and repetitive at once, loops that don’t evolve so much as they insist on themselves. Baby Ford‘s influence is audible in how minimal and slightly off-center the drum programming stays, that same stripped tension where less becomes the entire point rather than a limitation working against the track. “Murderer’s Row” leans into that same lineage even more directly, carrying an unintended tribute to Throbbing Gristle in its haze and darkness, deliberately murky where the rest of the EP stays brighter. It’s dance music built by someone who spent twenty years listening to other people make dance music, which sounds like it should produce something derivative and instead produces something oddly assured. He knows exactly which two or three elements a track actually needs and refuses to add a fourth just because he can.   Two EPs, two very different sounds :: Radius Etc‘s Alive & Thriving sits nowhere near that world. This is instrumental hip-hop pushed somewhere stranger, call it hip-hop IDM for lack of a cleaner label, though the term undersells how much dub techno and straight experimental electronic music bleeds into the beats underneath. Norwood recorded this across a blur of hostels, planes, and temporary housing between 2021 and 2025, and the press notes frame it explicitly as documentation of moving from housing instability and food scarcity into something closer to self-actualization. A travel document, in his own words, proof of surviving into thriving. That context sits underneath the music without ever being spelled out inside the tracks themselves, which is the right call. The record doesn’t lecture you about where it came from. It just carries the weight of it. “Goldenlocks” is the standout, and it’s also the most straightforwardly hip-hop beat on the record, except the tempo keeps breaking and the snares reverse and catch themselves mid-hit like the whole beat is tripping over its own feet on purpose. There’s a video for it, one of three the label produced for this release. Little vocal samples surface throughout, adding texture without ever becoming a hook. “Stuttering Spaces (PoplockJam)” goes fully electro, upbeat in a way nothing else on the record quite matches, the most purely fun three minutes here. “One 4 Larry Heard Pt. 1” is the only track running a straight 4/4 kick and it’s catchy specifically because it doesn’t try to be clever about it, same DNA as everything surrounding it just aimed squarely at a dancefloor instead of a headspace. The “Pt. 1” leaves you wondering if there’s a Pt. 2 coming or if the numbering is its own quiet joke about unfinished business. “Go Inside/Outside” is the most abstract piece on the record, a loop cycling endlessly through filters and phasers and pitch shifts like a revolving door that never fully closes, always mid-swing. The Consumers Research and Development Label is clearly not trying to be one thing, and that’s the most encouraging part of this reintroduction. A techno veteran finally putting out his own record after twenty years of platforming everyone else, sitting right next to a hip-hop travelogue built out of literal years of instability and constant movement, that’s a genuinely odd pairing on paper, and it works precisely because neither release is compromising to fit next to the other. They just happen to share a home. If these two EPs are the tone-setters for what Consumers wants to be in its second life, the label picked back up somewhere considerably more interesting than where it left off two decades ago. Drift‘s Manic and Radius Etc‘s Alive & Thriving are both available on The Consumers Research and Development Label. Manic by Drift    The post [2View] Drift :: Manic EP / Radius Etc :: Alive & Thriving EP (The Consumers Research and Development Label) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: Consumers Research and Development厂牌以两张风格迥异的EP重新出发，展现了独立厂牌的多元定位。Drift的《Manic》来自经营Parotic Records二十余年的Sean Krainik首次以个人名义发行的作品，融合techno与IDM元素，节拍厚重且面向舞池，循环段落执着于自身重复而拒绝演变，Baby Ford式的极简鼓机编程贯穿其中，标题曲以层叠构建脉动节拍配合电视对白形成微妙干扰。Radius Etc的《Alive & Thriving》则呈现为一段嘻哈旅行日志，记录了数年动荡与迁徙的经历。厂牌历经关闭、洪水损毁全部库存后于2024年正式重启，两张EP并列发行却互不妥协，这种奇异搭配反而构成了厂牌重生的核心张力。

items.excerpt: Analogical Force has long occupied the productive tension between experimentation and the dancefloor’s accumulated memory. Hidden Soul sits firmly within that tension, fluent in its established language and meticulously composed. But perhaps the most exciting possibility lies just beyond that fluency: not abandoning the listener, but trusting them enough to take the familiar somewhere unfamiliar. items.body: Analogical Force has long occupied the productive tension between experimentation and the dancefloor’s accumulated memory. Hidden Soul sits firmly within that tension, fluent in its established language and meticulously composed. But perhaps the most exciting possibility lies just beyond that fluency: not abandoning the listener, but trusting them enough to take the familiar somewhere unfamiliar. Muscle memory and accumulated emotional shorthand [AF069] Hidden Soul EP by The 89th Passenger   The 89th Passenger returns to the release schedule of one of contemporary dance music’s more compelling production houses with Hidden Soul, from Paris-based Jeremy Cohen delivering five tidy, DJ-friendly excursions into the familiar architecture of breaks, pads, subs and euphorically melancholic atmospheres. This is music that understands the dancefloor not as a problem requiring reinvention, but as an existing language, complete with its own grammar, muscle memory and accumulated emotional shorthand. “Paper Wings” establishes that grammar almost immediately. Chopped breaks, rounded subs, 303 squiggles and luminous pads are looped into clean, recognisable frames, each element occupying its expected orbit. There is something almost architectural about the neatness of it: familiar components assembled into a functioning environment designed to communicate quickly, cleanly and without obstruction. “Hidden Soul” pushes further into the low end, drawing on break patterns whose familiarity is part of their appeal. Its immediacy is hard to resist; the rhythmic language seems already lodged somewhere in the listener’s body. “What it Takes to Fly” lightens the palette considerably, pairing pretty 303 work with gorgeous tones and gently arpeggiating synths. Its carefully managed peaks, troughs and breakdowns possess an almost cinematic emotional shorthand—the kind of musical optimism that could soundtrack an airplane disappearing into a sunrise. Music interested in making the familiar feel good :: “Eren” continues along those coordinates, allowing textures to breathe while the rhythmic components settle into a quiet, efficient momentum. It feels less like a departure than another room in the same building: different light, familiar construction. “Analog Serenade” finally shifts the pace and texture again, suggesting another route through the material without substantially redrawing its map. And this is where the record becomes more interesting as an artefact of contemporary dance music. Its boundaries are visible. This is not music attempting to make the familiar unstable; it is music interested in making the familiar feel good. The breaks remain breaks, the 303 remains gloriously 303, and the emotional trajectory arrives largely where expectation has already placed it. There is safety here, but it is designed safety: a deliberate perimeter around the possibility of surprise. Yet accessibility and predictability are not the same thing. Music can push its own materials beyond their comfort zone without alienating the listener. In fact, some of the most generous dance music does precisely this, inviting you into a recognisable room before quietly moving the walls. Safety can be useful, but it can also become lazy—an easy creative cheat in which recognition performs the emotional labour that invention might otherwise have to do. Analogical Force has long occupied the productive tension between experimentation and the dancefloor’s accumulated memory. Hidden Soul sits firmly within that tension, fluent in its established language and meticulously composed. But perhaps the most exciting possibility lies just beyond that fluency: not abandoning the listener, but trusting them enough to take the familiar somewhere unfamiliar. Hidden Soul is available on Analogical Force. [Bandcamp] [AF069] Hidden Soul EP by The 89th PassengerThe post The 89th Passenger :: Hidden Soul EP (Analogical Force) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由巴黎制作人Jeremy Cohen以The 89th Passenger之名发行于Analogical Force厂牌，包含五首DJ导向的电子舞曲。评论指出作品大量使用碎拍、303酸性合成器、低频低音线和忧郁而明亮的合成器氛围，整体手法干净且高度可识别。乐评的核心论点在于这张专辑有意维持熟悉的舞曲语法而非颠覆它，碎拍仍是碎拍、303仍然是303，情绪走向也在预期之内。作者承认这种'设计过的安全感'带来了即时的感染力，但也指出专辑缺少令人意外的边界突破，仅在收尾的'Analog Serenade'中稍作纹理变化。综观而言，这是一张制作精良、面向舞池的电子作品，适合偏好熟悉音色语汇的听众，对追求结构创新的听者而言则略显保守。

items.body: Landscape 07 unfolds in breaths: slow waves advance, overlap, recede and return in subtly altered forms. The movement is continuous, yet it can escape a distracted listener. You need to stop, allow the piece to find its own pace and follow its changes as you might follow shadows moving across a field. An accomplished expression of stillness, physical presence and transformation landscape 07 by fields we found / quiet details   Fields We Found is the alias of British musician, mastering engineer and visual artist Alex Gold, who founded the quiet details label in 2023. Following releases on Home Normal, Seil Records, handstitched*, and Ambientologist, Gold has increasingly focused his work on extended listening. The Landscape series grew out of compositions created for his personal meditation practice; over time, the creative process itself also became a form of meditation. Landscape 07, the seventh installment in the series, runs for more than twenty-five minutes. It is an extended live performance constructed from electronic instruments, tape and successive layers of sound. The piece begins almost without a threshold. A broad sound emerges from the haze, already inhabited by tremors, gentle fluctuations and distant trails. During the opening minutes, the music gains weight; the volume rises calmly and glimmers of light move across its surface. From here, Landscape 07 unfolds in breaths: slow waves advance, overlap, recede and return in subtly altered forms. The movement is continuous, yet it can escape a distracted listener. You need to stop, allow the piece to find its own pace and follow its changes as you might follow shadows moving across a field. “Later, individual lines drift apart and the landscape opens out. This is where the title finds its true meaning. The horizon remains; the light changes. It is a slow transformation, free of spectacular gestures, shaped by passages that can be felt before they can be defined.” ~Mirco Salvadori The presence of tape can be felt in the sound’s internal movement. The notes have porous edges, slight instabilities and a warmth far removed from artificial stillness. Even when everything appears motionless, something continues to shift. The overall balance gradually changes, brighter colours surface and the mass of sound seems to lift. Later, individual lines drift apart and the landscape opens out. This is where the title finds its true meaning. The horizon remains; the light changes. It is a slow transformation, free of spectacular gestures, shaped by passages that can be felt before they can be defined. Gold handles duration with patience and restraint. Each event is allowed to remain long enough to alter our perception of everything around it. In its central section, the piece takes on a darker, more introspective colour. Threads and reflections continue to move through the texture; through headphones, they reveal small lateral movements, like currents. Light then returns gradually and the music expands without losing its composure. This leads to the point of greatest emotional intensity, reached through patient accumulation. The journey feels natural, almost as though it had formed by itself, while retaining the freedom of a gesture made in the moment. The piece asks for a simple kind of openness: to remain, to listen, to give each nuance time to reveal itself and to accept that the inner landscape may change alongside the sonic one. In these passages, distant echoes of German electronic music from the early 1970s begin to surface. The more abstract expanses of Tangerine Dream’s Zeit, the cosmic materiality of early Klaus Schulze and some of Cluster’s suspended atmospheres come to mind in the way timbre becomes form. Fields We Found keeps everything on an intimate, tactile scale. The connection lies in the trust placed in machines, in their natural drift and in the time a sound needs to reveal its hidden folds. Recording the performance directly to tape preserves the element of risk that gives life to such a gradual process. “A single sound remains, along with tape hiss and a few distant reflections; eventually, these elements also slip beneath the threshold of perception.” ~Mirco Salvadori An even closer affinity leads to Éliane Radigue. Landscape 07 shares the French composer’s attentiveness to what can emerge from within a prolonged sound and to the variations that appear when the ear stops searching for a melody. The historical and poetic distance remains clear; the surface here is denser and more explicitly ambient. Yet the kind of listening it requires is close to Radigue’s: focused, patient and ready to recognise an event within apparent stillness. Pauline Oliveros’ Deep Listening also comes to mind, particularly in its understanding of attention as an active part of the work, as does Suzanne Ciani, in the gentle way electronic sound can suggest physical movement. Towards the end, the piece begins to subtract. The pressure recedes, its lines grow sparse and what remains reveals its irregularities more clearly. The farewell becomes fragile. The long fade avoids any emphatic sense of closure. A single sound remains, along with tape hiss and a few distant reflections; eventually, these elements also slip beneath the threshold of perception. It is an ending fully consistent with the work as a whole: the ear is left to measure the disappearance, while the silence that follows seems to last a little longer. Landscape 07 succeeds because its calmness contains tension. Meditation here has density, pressure and material memory. The instruments breathe, the tapes impart instability and depth, and the studio work preserves the spontaneity of the performance. With each new listen, the hierarchy of details changes: something that first seemed marginal becomes a guide, a fluctuation turns into rhythm, a blur acquires definition. This is music that entrusts its richness to time and draws its strength from time in return. A remarkable entry in the series, and perhaps its most accomplished expression of stillness, physical presence and transformation. Landscape 07 is available on quiet details. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国音乐人Alex Gold（化名Fields We Found）Landscape系列的第七部作品，时长超过二十五分钟，源自其个人冥想练习的创作过程。作品以电子乐器、磁带和层层叠加的声音构建为一段现场演奏，几乎没有起始门槛，宽阔的音响从薄雾中浮现，内部带有细微的颤动和飘忽的轨迹。音乐在呼吸般的节奏中展开，慢波推进、重叠、退却，并以微妙变化的形态回归，呈现出一种静谧却持续变化的状态。磁带的特质体现在声音的多孔边缘和不稳定感中，即使表面静止，内部仍有流动。中段色彩转向更暗、更内省，光线随后逐渐回归，地平线依旧存在，光线持续改变。整个过程没有戏剧性的大动作，依靠可以被感知却难以定义的过渡来塑造。作品体现了对时长的耐心处理与克制，适合需要停下脚步、让音乐找到自身节奏的聆听方式。

items.body: Review by Agnenrecords — I was given the opportunity to review Jordan Rudess' WIRED FOR MADNESS before I'd ever listened to a note played by Dream Theater and equally shocking, I always used to skip over articles about the band in magazines and books. One good thing is that I was able to approach this review, for the keyboard player's fifteenth solo outing, without any idea of what the music would be like, although it's obvious that I've harboured preconceptions about the band he's most associated with. Another thing on the plus side, I know that Rudess is admired by musician friends whose opinions I respect, one of which lent Rudess his Kurzweil K2600 keyboard for a couple of performances organised by the Italian Dreamers during a Rudess family holiday in Italy around the time of Feeding the Wheel. The K2600 still bears Rudess' autograph. The album cover design neatly encapsulates the story behind the title track, an individual who accedes to becoming partially computerised and as his human self is reduced, he undergoes a procedure to upgrade his mental and physical capabilities. As a result he becomes increasingly separated from the outside world with his computerised portion performing the majority of his routine functions, allowing his mind to travel freely between madness and spiritual enlightenment. In a nod to previous prog epics, the track is split into two parts with a total running time of over 34 minutes and maintains a high tempo throughout. Without any Dream Theater reference points I have struggled to draw comparisons but in terms of wild, creative conceptuality and sheer musical density it comes close to Patrick Moraz's Story of i. It could easily have been dreamt up in 1974 and serves as a tribute to the 70's progressive rock keyboard players who influenced Rudess, Rick Wakeman, Keith Emerson and Patrick Moraz included. Having never heard his playing before I had no idea how good Rudess was, with elegant rhapsodic piano, authentic Hammond organ tones, and sinuous synthesizer runs. The modern sounding keyboards remind me of Eddie Jobson's work on the debut UK album and, when the rhythm section gets into a modern-jazz mood, like Dave Stewart on National Health's swansong DS al coda. I'm not a huge fan of the lyrics but they serve the composition well and, delivered by Rudess himself (apart from guest female vocals from Marjana Semkina in the role of an angel, and Dream Theater frontman James LaBrie at the climactic end to part 2), they are well sung. The track is heavy at times but there are sufficient strong melodies and tonal variation, almost all played at a frantic pace, to keep the listener interested. It goes without saying that his guest musicians are all of the highest calibre. With Wired for Madness parts 1 and 2 taking up more than half of the album and close enough to being able to fill a single traditional LP on their own, the remaining tracks run the risk of acting as filler, though this isn't really the case. Off the Ground is a straightforward pleasant, mellow, reflective piece, a welcome respite from the onslaught that's just taken place, but Drop Twist once again picks up the pace following an early arcade game-like intro. It may not be prog as we know it but the short instrumental allows Rudess to show his chops. Perpetual Shrine could almost be Drop Twist part 2, but if anything it's busier and funkier. It wouldn't sound out of place if it was used as the theme music for an 80s TV detective series based somewhere in Florida... The one track that feels to me to be there to make up the numbers is Just Can't Win. I'm being unfair because I'm not a fan of the Blues, but it performs a similar function to ELP's Tiger in a Spotlight, a moment of relief from the technical bombast but still a little self-indulgent. Here Rudess utilises the guitar talents of Joe Bonamassa and incorporates a full brass section; as a blues-rock song it can't be denied that it pushes all the appropriate buttons. Just for Today is another reflective, slow-paced number but it includes sweeping cinematic strokes before it gives way to the jazzy Why I Dream where the vocal phrasing reminds me of Supersister or Jeff Berlin on Gradually Going Tornado. Wired for Madness showcases Rudess' excellent playing and I believe he's pulled off something spectacular with the 34 minute title-track, an excess to rival anything from the 70s. It wasn't nearly as heavy as I'd feared but covers the whole gamut of prog and prog-related styles, with melody, rather than riff taking the lead. Furthermore, the pacy compositions that bookend the recording makes it sound as though the whole writing, playing and recording was fun. Three and a half stars

items._cn_summary: 这是Dream Theater键盘手Jordan Rudess的第十五张个人专辑，以三十四分钟的同名双联篇为核心概念作品。标题曲讲述一个半人半机的个体在疯狂与精神启蒙之间游离的故事，延续七十年代前卫摇滚键盘大师的遗产，融合Hammond风琴音色、钢琴狂想与合成器编织，节奏段带有现代爵士色彩。专辑被比作Patrick Moraz的史诗级作品，也让人联想到Eddie Jobson与Dave Stewart的键盘探索。除长篇主体外，其余短曲虽承担填充功能但并未流于敷衍。Marjana Semkina与James LaBrie担任客席人声，整体制作密集而旋律感强，速度始终维持在急促状态，对喜爱前卫摇滚与键盘叙事的听众具有吸引力。

items.body: German electro-industrial project Forma Tadre’s 1996 debut album “Navigator” is available on vinyl for the first time, as the opening release on the new label Analog Frontier. This 30th Anniversary Edition is a 2xLP gatefold pressed on 160g Electric Seaglass Blue vinyl, limited to 300 copies, and is sold through Analog Frontier’s Bandcamp page alongside a digital edition. Analog Frontier describes itself as a label dedicated to pressing CD and digital-only albums to vinyl for the first time, and “Navigator” is its debut release. The gatefold carries entirely new artwork built from period polar-expedition photography. The images include work by Herbert G. Ponting, official photographer of the British Antarctic (“Terra Nova”) expedition led by Robert Falcon Scott. The package also includes a double-sided insert with the album’s full lyrics. Side D of the vinyl edition adds two tracks that have never been released before: “First Land,” recorded in 1995, and “No Gene For Fate,” from 1997. Both date from the “Navigator” era of Forma Tadre’s catalogue. The 13-track edition runs: “Navigator (Part One)” “FX on a Human Subject” “Plasmasleep” “Date Unknown” “Navigator (Part Two)” “Serpent Charmer” “Looking Glass Men” “Mesozoic Tree Ferns” “Gates” “Celebrate the Cult” “Navigator (Part Three)” “First Land” “No Gene For Fate” “Navigator” was written, produced and mixed by Andreas Meyer, the sole member of Forma Tadre. Andreas Torkler handled mastering for the original eleven tracks. Meyer mastered “First Land” and “No Gene For Fate” himself, and Steve Eagle did additional mastering for the vinyl cut. B.A. Donahoo designed the new gatefold artwork, with additional art elements by Jared Cote and Steve Eagle. Hansjoerg Schifferer plays guitar on “Serpent Charmer” and “Celebrate the Cult.” The lacquer was cut at Complete Mastering and the vinyl pressed at Onyx Record Press. Originally released in 1996 on the German label Off Beat, “Navigator” was Meyer’s first release as the sole member of Forma Tadre. The album departed stylistically from the project’s earlier three-piece incarnation. “Navigator” centers on a theme of exploration and combines symphonic instrumental passages with EBM tracks. Meyer’s interest in the occult and in H.P. Lovecraft informed tracks including “Date Unknown,” “Celebrate the Cult,” “Gates” and “Mesozoic Tree Ferns.” The 30th Anniversary Edition is available as a digital album and as the limited vinyl edition on Bandcamp. Shipping of physical copies to the EU is currently on hold due to new EU customs policies. Navigator (30th Anniversary Edition) by Forma Tadre About Forma Tadre Forma Tadre began in 1986 as a three-piece band in Lower Saxony, Germany, with Andreas Meyer among its members. Meyer took the project’s name from a portmanteau of Tangerine Dream’s album “Force Majeure,” after Tangerine Dream’s “Phaedra” prompted him to buy his first synthesizer. The band played live and recorded the EP “Brightful Times” in 1987, produced by German producer Robert “Bobby” Giddens, who had also worked with DAF. Two of the three members subsequently left without recording further material. Meyer was the sole member of Forma Tadre by 1994. After the trio dissolved, Haujobb’s Björn Junemann encouraged Meyer to send demo tapes to record labels, which led Off Beat to sign him. In 1996, Meyer released “Navigator” as his first album under the Forma Tadre name, built partly from songs he had written separately from the band under the working title “P-Songs.” Around 1995, Meyer also worked with a female vocalist on a separate, classically-oriented project named Eisriesenkönig, which released a single track on Off Beat’s 1996 compilation “The O-Files.” After “Navigator,” Daniel Myer of Haujobb approached Meyer to collaborate, and the two formed Newt. The duo released two albums and a single between 1997 and 1999. Through the 1990s and 2000s, Meyer produced remixes for acts including Haujobb, La Floa Maldita, New Mind, Wumpscut and Assemblage 23. Forma Tadre’s second album, “Automate,” followed in 1998 and shifted toward a more ambient sound. After close to a decade of silence, Meyer returned Forma Tadre in 2008 with the 13-track album “The Music of Erich Zann,” inspired by H.P. Lovecraft’s short story of the same name. In 2019, “Brightful Times” was reissued as a hybrid vinyl-and-digital edition that added eight tracks recorded between 1987 and 1992 to the original four-track EP. In 2020, Forma Tadre released two archival anthologies. “Navigator Travelogue” collected remixes, singles, demos and unreleased tracks from 1994-1997, and “P-SongX, the hidden path” gathered personal recordings that predated “Navigator.” In 2021, Forma Tadre released “Geiger’s Day”, its first album issued on CD in 20 years. In 2025, the project followed with the digital archival compilation “Seven Century Factory”, which drew on demos and sketches recorded between 1997 and 2007. This reissue follows the 2019 vinyl-and-digital edition of “Brightful Times.” It extends Forma Tadre’s archival reissue campaign to “Navigator,” the project’s 1996 debut album.
items._cn_summary: 这是德国电子工业项目 Forma Tadre 1996 年首张专辑《Navigator》三十周年纪念版黑胶发行介绍。新版由新厂牌 Analog Frontier 首次压制成 2xLP gatefold 折叠封面，限量 300 张，采用电光海蓝色 160g 黑胶。封面美术取材于南极探险历史摄影，灵感来自 H.P. 洛夫克拉夫特及神秘主义主题。专辑融合交响器乐段落与 EBM 节拍，氛围冷峻且具有探索性叙事。三十周年版额外收录两首从未发表过的同年代曲目，数字版与黑胶版同步在 Bandcamp 上架。这篇内容本质上是一份黑胶发行新闻稿，详细列出制作人员、曲目列表与版本规格，但缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与听感分析。

items.body: Hermidgets, the anonymous Italian dark synthpop project, has released “Like Moths” alongside an official video. The single is out now through Bandcamp and is the fourth preview of Hermidgets’ third album, expected in early 2027. “Like Moths” was mixed by Matteo Sandri and mastered by Giovanni Versari. A bass-heavy opening gives way to rhythmic, buzzing synthesizers, with Hermidgets’ baritone vocal set against a danceable groove and a bright, wiry synth line that recurs through the track. The lyrics follow two people drawn into a relationship whose destructive pull has become part of its appeal, turning surrender into something close to devotional: “Learn how to pray for the pleasure of having nothing.” The video, directed around a concept developed independently of the song, was inspired by French artist Olivier de Sagazan. Shot in black and white, it isolates Hermidgets’ head and shoulders as white modeling clay obscures and distorts his features throughout the performance, with black pigment introduced later in the video. The project keeps its members unidentified, and the clay imagery extends that approach by withholding a clear view of the performer’s face. Like Moths by Hermidgets About Hermidgets Hermidgets is an Italian electronic project that does not identify its members, combining distorted synthpop and darkwave songwriting with self-produced visuals. The debut album, “The Mire,” was released in November 2020 and included the songs “This Is Over” and “Nothing’s Perfect.” The singles “A Flaw” and “Perks” followed in 2021, and “Meaninglessness” and “We Tend to Disappear” appeared on the mini-album “NIHIL” in June 2024, recorded with a limited setup of two analog synthesizers, drum samples and voice. Hermidgets began previewing a third album with the single “Fall Apart” in July 2025, followed by “Sundown” in December 2025 and “Could I Be Better” in March 2026, a song that revisits “Could Be Better” from the 2020 debut. “Like Moths,” released in September 2026, is the fourth single from that album cycle, with the full album expected in early 2027.
items._cn_summary: Hermidgets 是一支匿名的意大利暗潮电子项目，2026年9月发行单曲《Like Moths》，作为其第三张专辑（预计2027年初发行）的第四首先行曲。音乐以低音主导的开场切入，搭配蜂鸣感的节奏合成器与男中音人声，整体旋律具有舞曲律动感，明亮细瘦的合成器线条贯穿全曲。歌词聚焦于两个人被一段具有破坏性的关系吸引，将屈服演变为近乎虔诚的仪式感。MV以黑白影像呈现，受法国艺术家Olivier de Sagazan启发，以白色雕塑泥土逐渐覆盖和扭曲表演者面部，黑色颜料在后期引入，强化了项目刻意隐藏成员身份的概念。制作方面由Matteo Sandri混音、Giovanni Versari母带处理。整体延续了项目自2020年首张专辑《The Mire》以来将扭曲合成器流行与暗潮写作结合的路线，并在视觉层面以手工黏土装置延伸其匿名美学。

items.body: Susanne Jonsson and Jan Strandqvist of the Swedish band Red Mecca have returned after a hiatus. Their time away, however, was marked by intense and deeply painful experiences: Susanne’s sister was murdered and her relationship fell apart, while Jan struggled with addiction. Sometimes, nothing seems better than returning to creative expression—in their case, by making a new album. This record clearly holds great significance for them, even though the music remains true to Red Mecca’s signature sound and style. It is a polished album, balancing understated, sensitive, and refined tracks with a somewhat ‘harder’ Synth-Pop style. The songs are expertly crafted and beautifully sung by Susanne Jonsson, a vocalist who has nothing left to prove. Personally, I prefer their Electro-Pop style—which occasionally hints at EBM elements—as it really showcases their talent for creating great music. While some tracks may lack a definitive climax, I believe the choice to create a more restrained work was deliberate. This may not be my favorite album by the duo, but it stands as a significant and healing production in their career. (Rating:7½). Listen to “I’m On The Outside”: I’m On The Outside by Red Mecca About Red Mecca Red Mecca was set up by Jan Strandqvist, originally with vocalist Frida Madeleine, who left after four albums and was replaced by Susanne Jonsson. The Swedish duo released “Truth” in 2019, followed by the albums “Away” (2021) and “Stay” (2023), all on Massproduktion. Strandqvist discussed the band’s history, including a 2016 Swedish Manifest Award win and a soundtrack placement on “Killing Eve”, in a 2021 Side-Line Click Interview.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典二人组Red Mecca在经历了成员个人创伤后回归，专辑呈现克制内敛的氛围，精致打磨的合成器流行与偶尔浮现的EBM元素交替推进。Susanne Jonsson的演唱沉稳而有层次，编曲在敏感细腻段落与稍硬的电子节拍之间寻求平衡。整体选择了一种有意识的节制表达，部分曲目缺乏明确的情绪高点，但作为创伤后的疗愈之作，其内省特质贯穿始终。制作上延续了乐队一贯的Electro-Pop路线，没有大幅突破，但在合成器音色与人声编排的配合上展现出成熟把控。独立厂牌Massproduktion发行，保持了地下电子乐的制作理念。这张专辑更适合在安静夜晚独自聆听，而非舞池场景。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由小提琴家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，延续其此前OĽUN项目中将斯洛伐克传统音乐与古典音乐相融合的思路。三组音乐家参与：弦乐四重奏Spectrum Quartett、传统器乐四人组Nogaband（由小提琴手Michal Noga领衔，含低音提琴与和弦中提琴），以及女声演唱组Ulijanky。曲目多为对斯洛伐克作曲家Eugen Suchoň、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes及曾深入斯洛伐克采风的匈牙利作曲家Bartók作品的重新诠释。每一首的创作素材均注明源自斯洛伐克各村庄的具体音乐家与地点，编排与表演保留传统人声音色与原始能量，并非管弦乐化的平滑处理。评论者认为演奏与演唱兼具传统音乐的精神、技巧与匠心。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这是一张关于墨西哥牛仔（vaquero）与夏威夷牧牛人（paniolo）历史渊源的文化跨界专辑。十九世纪墨西哥人从加州前往夏威夷岛屿放牧长角牛，同时将吉他带入当地，由此衍生出独特的音乐交融脉络。专辑收录十六首曲目，将西班牙语与夏威夷语歌曲重新配词，混合原创与传统美洲民谣，以尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴与手风琴为骨架编排出密集层次。Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo作为核心催化者参与编曲和器乐演奏，另有夏威夷本土艺人Gary Haleamau、Sonny Lim等参与人声合作。录制在加州圣保罗的工作室一间房间内同期完成，邀请学院学生一同参演，展现出丰富的语言、文化、年龄与性别多元协作。曲目中包含Woody Guthrie《Deportee》的社会评论性诠释，以及充满即兴段落的器乐展开，整体呈现出文化对话的厚度与现场演奏的自发活力。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合 GuldGanger 的首张数字 EP，由北欧民谣圈资深歌手 Mia Guldhammer 主唱。五首曲目大多取材于传统音乐，演奏者各自带来不同诠释视角，整体弥漫着古老而粗粝的氛围。开篇曲《Svennedal》以粗犷的奔跑节奏展示主唱极具说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目《Nordgård》由乐队成员 Morten Musicus 创作，口簧与风笛提供强劲推动力。传统曲《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以扬琴为底，音色细腻；终曲《Orms》作为器乐曲，融合口簧、长笛与弦乐，产生活泼而略带失衡的奇特效果。作为一张引介之作，乐队展现出超越新人水准的成熟度，但数字 EP 的容量和传统民谣的基底使其在实验性方面仍有探索空间。

It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这是一张在芝加哥南区街头录制的田野录音作品，由录音师Ian Brennan操刀，邀请25位枪支暴力幸存者参与，年龄从17岁到67岁不等。录音地点选在一位94岁祖母家门前，正值特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻该市当天。作品本身并非传统音乐，而是一份关于暴力、社区创伤与社会不平等的声音文献。一位痛失两子的老人在录音中情绪崩溃，反复道歉——这种脆弱的真实感远超刻意制作的音乐。文中提及南区曾是Muddy Waters、Willie Dixon、Howlin' Wolf等蓝调传奇和Lionel Hampton等爵士音乐家的发源地，与今日的暴力现实形成强烈对照。全部收益将捐给Cure Violence Global组织。作为实验性声音艺术和田野录音，它与用户口味中的实验/前卫部分有一定契合，但更偏向社会纪实而非纯音乐创作。

items.body: Swedish duo Svaj. released a remix of the alan is waiting track “where you disappear” on 2 October 2026. The one-track single, titled “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild),” streams on Spotify and is available for download on Bandcamp and Subvert. The original song was written and sung by alan is waiting, the recording name of a Stockholm-based electronic artist whose debut album, “The Last of You,” came out in 2024. Svaj., the duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg based in Blackeberg, Stockholm, reworked the track for the remix. The release keeps alan is waiting’s original vocals. In a newsletter announcement, Svaj. described the result as “a wonky, New Order-tinged full-on synth-pop hit song.” where you disappear – Svaj. rebuild by Svaj., alan is waiting A visualizer for “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” is available on YouTube. About Svaj. Svaj. is the Stockholm duo of Anders O Öhgren and Tomas Z Westberg, based in the Blackeberg district of the city. The duo releases through its own TZW Produktion imprint. Svaj.’s Bandcamp profile describes its sound as “voice, electronics and bass. Minimal, experimental and industrial, yet melodic and danceable,” and compares it to Joy Division and Front 242. Svaj. issued its debut EP, “Rewind,” in March 2022. The songs reworked tracks originally recorded on tape in 1988, revisited with a Yamaha CS-10 synthesizer and a 1960s Tandberg reel-to-reel recorder. The duo’s second release, “Until We Fall,” followed in 2023. In 2024, Svaj. released the single “Cut Me Up,” a reworking of a song first written by Alien Waveform in 1989 and later issued as “Contagion” on the 1993 compilation “Tapping the Wires (A Selection of Futuristic Electro Mindbeats).” The digital single included a remix by UK industrial act Portion Control. The same year, Svaj. contributed “Brända Barn,” a reworking of a 1980 Swedish punk song, to the six-act compilation “SVÄRTA.” Svaj. released its third collection, “Maggots,” a six-track release, on 17 May 2025 through TZW Produktion on vinyl, CD and digital formats. The record includes a cover of John Cale’s 1974 track “Fear Is a Man’s Best Friend” and features contributions from Perra Wikström on contrabass and guitar and vocal effects from Devoid. Svaj. issued four music videos from “Maggots” through 2025, for “Experience,” “Fear,” “Portent” and, in October 2025, “Piglet.” The duo released the single “Patterns” on 19 February 2026. Svaj.’s catalog now runs from the 2022 “Rewind” EP through this month’s “where you disappear (Svaj. Rebuild)” remix.
items._cn_summary: 瑞典双人组 Svaj. 重新混音了斯德哥尔摩电子艺术家 alan is waiting 的单曲 "where you disappear"，保留了原曲人声，以合成器为主导进行重构，自称为带有 New Order 质感的合成器流行作品。Svaj. 的音乐根基偏向暗黑氛围与工业电子，擅长以 Yamaha CS-10 合成器和复古磁带录音设备重新处理老素材，作品常被比作 Joy Division 与 Front 242。两位成员来自斯德哥尔摩 Blackeberg 区，通过自有厂牌 TZW Produktion 发行，此前曾改编 1980 年代瑞典朋克与 1988 年磁带录音作品。此次 remix 延续其解构与再构建的创作思路，将原曲人声置入其标志性的极简实验电子框架中，融合旋律性与机械律动。整体定位介于暗潮、工业与合成器流行之间，适合偏好实验电子与后朋克交叉地带的小众听众。

items.body: Toronto-based guitarist, Ayal Senior, developed an approach of listening, playing and collaborating deeply, unhurried and with space (hence the title ‘Yutori‘, which translates to ‘space’) after several creative sojourns to Japan. This philosophy of taking time and patience to create comes through the record’s immeansly laid-back and tranquil dream-folk vibes. The album grew out of of a hushed winter morning session in the recording studio with Senior and several of his friends and collaborators leaning into this almost zen-like method of playing and being in tune with each other. The music’s vast openness and meditative qualities reflect the nature of these sessions, giving them the loose and communal feeling of tight improvised jams. This cooperative energy gives the record a sense of excitement, as it gives the impression the songs can go into any direction at any time. So your ear and attention are hooked right away, and they remain held til the needle reaches the deadwax on Side B. Throughout the album, you are treated to unique variations of instrumental ambient folk that splinters into cosmic string music and astral Americana sounds, with spacey pedal steel, acoustic and fried electric guitar, pearly vibraphones and warm cello. Some tracks are like mini-baroque symphonies, while others lean more into the psychedelic, with dreamlike atmospheric passages and stream of consciousness-styled distorted soloing. The record has the ambiance of a Nick Drake LP, but paired with the looseness and cosmic expansiveness of a Matt Valentine or even a Popol Vuh album. This is especially true with the track that finishes out Side A, “Well of Seven.” Yutori is as serene as a day spent floating around in a still pond, as pastoral as a walk through a freshly snow-covered forest and as illusory and wistful as a half-remembered daydream. If you need a bucolic and peaceful listen to soundtrack your autumn, then this is the album you should reach for. Click here to get your copy on vinyl or digital today. -KH
items._genre: ambient folk / dream-folk / instrumental / cosmic Americana
items._cn_summary: 多伦多吉他手 Ayal Senior 多次赴日本创作后，将'余裕'（yutori，日语意为空间）的理念注入这张专辑。整张唱片源于冬季录音室中与几位伙伴的安静晨间即兴，呈现出松散而公社化的合奏氛围，乐曲走向自由开放，引人持续聆听。专辑融合器乐氛围民谣、宇宙弦乐与星空美式风格，配器涵盖滑棒吉他、原声与失真电吉他、颤音琴与温暖大提琴。部分段落近似巴洛克小交响曲，另一些则偏向迷幻氛围与意识流式独奏，整体气质兼具 Nick Drake 的宁静与 Popol Vuh 的宇宙感。作为秋季聆听推荐，专辑适合追求宁静氛围与即兴美感的听众，但缺少更深层的实验突破。

items.body: Out of all of the underrated bands I know, Boss Keloid have to be among the most underrated. They have many virtues I could sing but the main one is that they just sound like no one else. Their type of winding, dense, and uniquely harmonic stoner/progressive rock is just inimitable. And so, I live between Keloid to Keloid release, craving the very specific flavor that only they can provide. Happily, my latest fix is almost here and good lord is it glorious! Float & Aperture leaves behind a lot of the size and grandiosity of Family The Smiling Thrush and the density of Melted On the Inch in favor of a hard to pin down etherealness. "Pedestal", the second track which I am very pleased to premiere here, will do a better job at explaining what I mean than I can. Check it out below. Float & Aperture by Boss Keloid God, I just love this band. On "Pedestal" you get a taste of the leitmotif which runs through the entire album, some strangely (and pleasingly) sweet, high pitched vocals, and a whole lot of that sound palette that makes Boss Keloid who they are. Which is what exactly? It's that insidious lead guitar line, the fact that I could mean any of the three (at my count) lead guitar lines, the bubbling bass, the way the whole thing feels off-kilter, hazy, and psychedelic to such a unique degree. And finally, it's the excellent lyrics, here (like on the rest of the album) turned very introverted, musing on meaning, intent, self-knowledge, and failure.The entire release is this good. Like "Pedestal", it's angry at times. At others it's alluring, fantastical, strange, self-flagellating, self-aggrandizing, and a few dozens other emotions and perspectives besides. It's similar to previous Keloid releases but also different, uniquely its own thing just like all of their other albums. God I love this band. Please listen to this band! The full thing drops on October 23rd and you can, and should, pre-order it from the Bandcamp page above.
items._cn_summary: 乐评介绍了Boss Keloid新专辑《Float & Aperture》中的单曲《Pedestal》。作者认为该乐队是被严重低估的组合，其音乐风格蜿蜒绵密、和声独特，在stoner rock与前卫摇滚之间开辟出难以模仿的声音路径。新作相较前作减少了大体量与繁复密度，转向难以定义的空灵质感。歌曲中包含贯穿全专辑的主导动机、高亢甜美的人声、隐晦而具辨识度的领奏吉他线、起伏有致的贝斯律动，整体氛围失衡、朦胧且高度迷幻。歌词转向内向反思，探讨意义、意图、自我认知与失败等主题。专辑情绪多变，时而愤怒，时而诱人、奇幻、自我鞭挞、自我膨胀，展现出独立而完整的艺术面貌。

items.body: Review by Agnenrecords — Echorec featured in Prog magazine 106 (February 2020) in an article titled 16 bands to watch this year, before their debut album The Island had even been released. Currently based in Bath, the trio easily deserve a place in that list because The Island is an incredibly mature offering. They even had the audacity to attempt, and successfully pull off a subtle interpretation of the end section of Pink Floyd's Echoes during the 17 minute long closing track The Lamb Returns ? Pink Floyd, listed as 'an artist we also like', being one of the leading exponents of the Binson Echorec analogue delay effect which provided the young band with their name. Made up of Julian Kirk (vocals, guitars and keyboards), Brad McGinty (bass, vocals) and Jake Aubrey (drums and percussion), there's no compromise in the quality or quantity of either lead instrument; Kirk is a genuine multi-instrumentalist who can play stately Gilmour-like guitar but also does an admirable impersonation of Tony Banks playing a fluid ARP solo on The Cinema Show. Despite being momentarily reminded of David Surkamp on Safe at Home (the epigrammatic opener The Water is a piano instrumental) I declined to look for comparisons with Kirk's vocal style because his voice simply seems to fit well with the music. McGinty and Aubrey are also both very capable musicians, meting out inventive rhythm patterns during staccato riffing or bubbling and bouncing along in the melodic sections - this is the essence of the music, it's primarily melodic, it's not derivative, it has plenty of changes and uses a broad palette to produce a nicely-balanced modern prog sound with classic touches.The Island is a concept album that relates the story of a teenage girl's journey of self-discovery. Raised on a lighthouse rock by a single mother who is reluctant to grant her any freedom, she flees to the Island in search of her father. The truth is finally revealed in the epic The Lamb Returns, that her nuclear family fell apart following the early death of her older brother. It's hard to believe that the story isn't personal ? it's well constructed with suitable imagery of yearning, hope, doubt and resolution ? and it's certainly a bold move on a debut release.It's not really a big issue because the entire work is thoroughly commendable, but I don't think the lyrics, which work fine as part of individual song structures and as an overarching narrative, fully rise to the challenge of telling such difficult themes.Stuck in the middle of a pandemic, a streaming-only release is not unreasonable, though getting noticed in a vast industry geared towards rewarding established acts and/or instant gratification isn't going to be easy for a new band with a debut album. In my opinion, the interest generated by exposure through Prog magazine should be maximised by investing in a physical product to be ready for the merchandise stand when gigs resume. I'm pretty sure that Echorec's music will be greeted favourably by the prog community.Three and a half stars
items._cn_summary: ECHOREC由Julian Kirk（人声、吉他、键盘）、Brad McGinty（贝斯、人声）和Jake Aubrey（鼓）三人组成，首张专辑《The Island》以一位少女逃离灯塔追寻父亲的成长叙事为概念主线，十七分钟长的尾曲《The Lamb Returns》揭示了家庭解体的真相。音乐以旋律性为基调，节奏段落富含变化，吉他音色带有Gilmour式的庄重感，键盘段落则流露出Tony Banks的影响，结尾段落巧妙化用Pink Floyd《Echoes》的余韵。整体呈现一种融入经典触感的现代前卫摇滚风格，编曲精致，乐队成员演奏技术扎实，乐评认为作品在叙事深度上仍有提升空间。专辑在疫情期仅以流媒体形式发行，乐评建议乐队应为演出恢复后的实体产品做好准备。

items.body: Mass Minor, the Austin, Texas-based darkwave and electronic rock project of Andrew J. Martin Jr., released the single “Get Up” on 2 October 2026 via Metropolis Records. Get Up by Mass Minor “This song is a conversation with God at 169 BPM about sin, money, mortality and the things we sacrifice our lives to,” Martin says of the track. “It comes from this idea of asking God to save us from problems we created ourselves. Maybe it’s not God’s job to save us. Maybe we need to fix our own shit. You’re the one holding the light. Get up.” A music video for “Get Up”, directed by Teresa Jolie and edited by Beau Loy, accompanies the release. “Get Up” follows “Nowhere Now”, issued as a single in late July. Both songs are set to appear on a new Mass Minor album, “Beyond The Edge Of Reason”, due out in late February 2027 on Metropolis Records. About Mass Minor Mass Minor is the Austin, Texas-based project of Andrew J. Martin Jr., who blends atmospheric synths and driving guitars with post-punk, synth-pop and alternative rock influences. Martin self-released the project’s debut album, “Become Each Other”, in 2020, followed by a run of singles later collected on EPs. The project built a presence in the dark alternative scene through radio support, multiple SXSW appearances and shows alongside acts including Twin Tribes, Ultra Sunn, TRAITRS, Vision Video, Urban Heat and Sacred Skin. Mass Minor signed to Metropolis Records and released the single “Nowhere Now” in July 2026, followed by “Get Up” on 2 October 2026. Both tracks lead into the project’s next album, “Beyond The Edge Of Reason”, due in late February 2027.

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of

items.body:
For XD:I, the show extends well beyond a three-minute song.

Made up of SWAN, BETTY, HAZÈ, and KANA, the four-member girl group combine K-pop vocals, rap, and choreography with DJing and electronic music. Their live format revolves around a continuous set, with members moving between the decks and the main stage as they build the crowd’s energy.

Represented by THE ARK Foundation, XD:I have been developing that approach through club and party performances in Seoul, including a 40-minute live set at Jangchung Gymnasium in August. Their recent festival bookings included EDC Korea’s circuitGROUNDS stage on 3 October, bringing the project into the electronic music festival circuit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by XD:I (@way2_xdi)

K-pop listeners may already recognise SWAN as Shin Jiyoon, formerly of Weeekly. A songwriter and composer as well as a performer, she brings her idol experience into a role that now includes DJing and longer festival sets. Her artist profile also details solo work spanning lyric writing, composition, arrangement, choreography, and styling.

Alongside her at the decks is BETTY, whose background includes club appearances and a runner-up placing at the PLIT DJ Competition. She moves between DJing, rap, MCing, and dance, helping maintain momentum and respond to the audience throughout the set.

HAZÈ adds vocals, rap, and performance to the mix. Her profile describes a more restrained approach to expression, offering a different presence within the group. Youngest member KANA contributes vocals and dance, highlighted by her clear vocal tone and expressive delivery.

Those individual strengths feed into a flexible approach to performing. SWAN and BETTY handle DJing, while all four contribute across the show, with their roles changing according to the track and the flow of the set. Songs connect through electronic sections, choreography, and crowd interaction, giving the members room to develop a performance over a longer stretch of time.

“XD:I has been developed as a group that can connect DJing, vocals, rap, choreography, performance and direct audience interaction within one continuous set,” says Chanjae Park, CEO of THE ARK Foundation. “Each member has a different strength, and those different strengths come together to create the full XD:I live experience.”

For an introduction to their recorded music, there’s ‘SPRAY U’. Released on 5 August, the tech house-based single establishes the electronic direction underpinning the group’s live concept.

XD:I plan to take that format to more clubs and international festivals while continuing to release music as a K-pop group. Their ambition is to make the transitions between the decks, the microphone, and the choreography part of what fans come to see.

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Throughout his career, Jon Anderson has not limited himself to the paths of progressive rock. His constant exploration of diverse musical languages - in search of new textures and nuances and free from conventional constraints - has led him to expand his sonic palette and reflect it in musical works of very different natures. "The More You Know" (1998), his twelfth studio album, is one of those works that strays furthest from the genre that made Yes one of its leading standard-bearers.Prioritizing gentle, melodic structures over any display of instrumental virtuosity, "The More You Know" moves, almost effortlessly, through pop and world music sounds, in which the arrangements and programming form the foundation upon which much of the album rests. Songs like "Magic Love," "Say Jocky," and "Take, Take, Take" are easy on the ears but don't seem to offer anything substantial. On the other hand, when the English singer's more spiritual side comes to the fore, some of the album's best moments emerge, including the melancholic "Heaven's Love" and "Sad," and the jubilant "Youth" with its ethnic overtones.Also noteworthy are the arrangements on "Dancing Fool" and the light soul-jazz of "Free (Some Would Say)," underpinned by the deep, expressive bass of Bobby Jocky, brother of Francis Jocky, who contributes on keyboards and as a composer. The rest of the album hovers in an accessible average that never quite takes off, with the standout feature being Anderson's angelic voice, which is in fine form. That's no small thing, but it's not enough to overcome a production that, at times, feels overly polished.2/2.5 stars
items._cn_summary: Jon Anderson作为Yes乐队主音歌手，在这张个人专辑中彻底脱离了前卫摇滚路线，转向以轻柔旋律为主的流行与世界音乐融合。整张专辑依赖编曲与电子编程构建基底，放弃了器乐炫技。部分曲目如《Heaven's Love》《Youth》展现了其精神性的一面，带有民族色彩与忧郁气质；《Free (Some Would Say)》呈现轻爵士灵魂风味。评论指出多首歌曲虽悦耳但缺乏实质内容，Anderson天使般的嗓音是最大亮点，但整体制作有时显得过度抛光。

items.body: Darkmechanic released the album “Hypercontrol” on 2 October 2026 through the Slovak label Aliens Production. The eight-track record is the industrial electronic project’s second album and its first release for the label. Alexander Borsov, who records as Darkmechanic, wrote, produced and mastered all eight tracks. “Hypercontrol” comprises: The deceitful idol Puppet Gloomy lake Cau the night cult Hypercontrol Go all….F Resolving a controversy Halloween (Bonus track) Aliens Production describes the album as “a mechanical colossus of industrial energy and electronic flashes.” “Hypercontrol” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp. Aliens Production is a Slovak dark electronics label operating since 1997. Side-Line has previously covered Aliens Production releases by the Polish electro/EBM act Fractal, including “Antidote” in 2023 and “Hide in the light” in 2026, both on the same label. Hypercontrol by Darkmechanic About Darkmechanic Darkmechanic is the solo industrial electronic project of Alexander Borsov, who also records as Dark The Keeper and Stellar Dynamics. The project’s first recorded appearance was a track on the compilation “Dark Virus X-Mas”, released by Russian Dark Community in 2020. Darkmechanic’s debut album, “Ghost Reflection”, followed in 2021, also through Russian Dark Community. Between albums, Borsov contributed remixes to other artists’ releases: “Blood For Blood Remixes” (2023) on DSBP, “Monolith” (2023) by Reagent, “Mvrtyr” (2024) by G.G.F.H. and “Lost EP” (2025) by Synaptic Defect. Darkmechanic also appeared on the compilation “Cyclone Front: Movements and Currents” in 2025. “Hypercontrol”, released on 2 October 2026, is Darkmechanic’s second album and the project’s first release through Aliens Production, five years after “Ghost Reflection”.

items.body: Cry DOPE, a dark electro-pop duo from Tokyo, released its debut digital single “Dark Dopamine” on October 2, 2026. The duo, Syuri and Sonar, sing in both Japanese and English across the track’s 3:03 running time. An official music video followed on YouTube on October 3. The track’s chorus alternates “Han-bun, han-bun, han-bun-bun” (“half, half, half-half”) in Japanese with the English line “Half of me is still asleep.” Each verse plays out as a short back-and-forth: an unfamiliar key in the mailbox, a letter on the fridge that reads only “sorry,” and questions about a name, the time, and whether to go home. The music is as far as we can gather AI assisted or generated. “Dark Dopamine” streams on Spotify, Apple Music and other platforms. About Cry DOPE Cry DOPE is the Tokyo-based duo of Syuri and Sonar. The band describes its sound as music that “sits somewhere between a late-night room and the city outside,” sung in both Japanese and English. “Dark Dopamine,” released October 2, 2026, is the duo’s debut single.
