items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items.body: While the title of Sandrine Piau and David Kadouch’s new project translates to “tales,” the performers in their accompanying interview note the complexity of their theme: light and dark tales, they observe, follow us into adulthood, creating a multidimensional way to tell stories. Contes Amazon Presto Apple The offerings here are indeed diverse: Piau plays to her strengths in French art song but also extends her range to include songs by Wolf and Shostakovich. Jeanne Bernard’s Trois chansons de Bilitis opens the program; this set is not to be confused with Debussy’s more famous cycle. The songs themselves are based on entirely different poems from Pierre Louÿs’ collection, with Debussy choosing themes of sensual love and nature. Bernard, on the other hand, elects to depict scenes of childhood and innocence. It’s a shame that her version is so often overshadowed, as it is a delightful cycle. Piau’s vocal timbre and temperament fit beautifully, breathing much vitality into the songs. Les petits enfants (track 1) is effusive and imaginative, while Les contes (track 2) takes a gentler turn. Several times, the textures thin to a single line in each part, and the duo creates a beautiful tenderness in such moments. Reynaldo Hahn’s À Chloris (track 4) draws unmistakably upon Baroque styles. Piau’s familiarity with this repertoire through her extensive Baroque discography serves her well: her vocal control is not just meticulous but reveals an exquisite level of clarity. In some ways, I found that her voice takes on an almost flute- or recorder-like quality. Kadouch’s accompaniment possesses a similar pristine quality but also brings a sense of placid warmth. Wally Karveno’s La robe de lune (track 5) is a quirky waltz that vacillates between the lush and bold and the quiet and introspective. The performers capture the spirit of each character without losing the anticipation the text conveys. The ending, though, offers a moment of unexpected irony: the warmth the duo evokes at the arrival of the major key actually speaks to the saddest moment in the poem. La fille aux cheveux de lin (track 6) gives Kadouch a solo moment. Consistent with his duo playing, his style is uncontrived and speaks directly to the listener. However, parts of Debussy’s prelude could use a little more time to let the harmonies bloom or for the color changes to work their full magic. Maurice Ravel’s Cinq mélodies populaires grecques is a series of five vignettes of traditional Greek life and features some of the most vivacious and sensitive performances from the duo. The excitement of a wedding morning comes through Piau’s breathy phrases and Kadouch’s delicate chimes, vividly reminiscent of wedding bells in the distance. The words of Là-bas, vers l’église (track 8) may be relatively simple, but the performance says otherwise: Kadouch’s opening chords create a nuanced sparkle while Piau brings a new level of expanse and resonance to her lines. The folk element is alive and well in Quel galant m’est comparable (track 9) but without losing the refinement of Ravel’s musical style. Sandrine Piau and David Kadouch. Photo © Sandrine Expilly. Among the non-French repertoire, Hugo Wolf’s Die Geister am Mummelsee (track 13) from the Mörike-Lieder shows a different side of Piau’s vocal profile. Up to this point, her light coloratura range has featured prominently, but this song brings out a warmer, lyric quality. It holds up very well even over Kadouch’s thicker accompaniment, which also allows the pianist to unleash a fuller, more powerful sound we’ve not yet heard. One of the best selections on the album is Richard Strauss’ Wiegenlied (track 14), whose ebullience is captured in the piano part that mimics flowing water. Meanwhile, Piau assumes a presence that draws on both her strengths—high-register clarity and middle-register glow—to create a highly expressive narrative. Shostakovich’s Ophelia’s Song (track 26) is the album’s emotional low point, though it comes a little too late in the program. Still, it’s a welcome contrast to the lighter songs. The most striking difference from the other songs is the scoring for voice and cello. The poignancy of the string instrument brings an added level of desolation to the music. Piau once again turns to her lyric timbre here in an interpretation that is both soulful and devastating. Contes is yet another well-programmed and thoughtfully rendered album from Piau and her collaborators, and one that showcases her expressive versatility. Warmly recommended. items.body: English post-punk band Killing Joke released their self-titled debut album, “Killing Joke,” on 5 October 1980 through E.G. Records, distributed by Polydor Records. The record turns 46 this year. Killing Joke recorded the album in August 1980 at Marquee Studios in London and produced it themselves, with Phil Harding as engineer. Drummer Paul Ferguson described the sessions as recorded live with “no overdubs to speak of.” The eight-track UK LP runs: “Requiem” “Wardance” “Tomorrow’s World” “Bloodsport” “The Wait” “Complications” “S.O.36” “Primitive” The original US pressing added “Change,” the B-side of the “Requiem” single, between “Complications” and “S.O.36.” “Wardance” came out as a single in February 1980, ahead of the album, and “Requiem” followed as a single in September 1980. The album entered the UK Albums Chart on 25 October 1980 at number 41 and later peaked at number 39. Its cover collages a photograph by Don McCullin of CS gas clashes in Derry, Northern Ireland, in 1971, designed by Mike Coles. In 2019, Pitchfork placed the album at number 9 on its list of the 33 best industrial albums of all time. “The Wait” was covered by Metallica on the 1987 “Garage Days Re-Revisited” EP and later included on “Garage Inc.,” “Primitive” was covered by Helmet in 1993, and “Requiem” was covered by Foo Fighters in 1997 as a B-side to “Everlong.” About Killing Joke Killing Joke formed in October 1978 in Notting Hill, London. Jaz Coleman (vocals, keyboards) and Paul Ferguson (drums) met in late 1978 and placed an announcement in Melody Maker in February 1979 reading “Bass, lead, to tell the killing joke, we mean it man!” Guitarist Geordie Walker and bassist Martin “Youth” Glover answered and completed the original line-up. The band released its debut EP, “Turn to Red,” as a 10-inch on 26 October 1979 on Malicious Damage, the label Killing Joke ran with graphic artist Mike Coles. Recorded in August 1979 at Gooseberry Sound in London, the EP drew airplay from BBC Radio 1’s John Peel. The “Almost Red” EP followed that November, and the single “Nervous System,” with “Turn to Red” as its B-side, came out in December 1979. Killing Joke then signed to E.G. Records for the self-titled debut album, released on 5 October 1980. The band’s next albums were “What’s THIS For…!” (1981) and “Revelations” (1982), after which Youth left the band and was replaced by Paul Raven on bass. “Fire Dances” followed in 1983 and “Night Time” in 1985, the album that carried the single “Love Like Blood” and brought the band its widest chart exposure to date. Killing Joke continued recording and touring into the 2010s with albums including “Absolute Dissent” (2010), “MMXII” (2012) and “Pylon” (2015), with Jaz Coleman and Geordie Walker as the group’s only constant members. Geordie Walker died in November 2023 at the age of 64, as Side-Line reported at the time. The band’s 1980 debut album remains the record that introduced the Killing Joke sound now marking its 46th anniversary this October.

items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail released the single “Vile Train” on 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The track is the first digital single from the band’s forthcoming full-length album “Infinite Fountain,” set for release on 6 November 2026 through the same French label. A video for “Vile Train” accompanies the single. Night Nail’s Brandon Robert wrote “Vile Train” after a visit to the ash-covered ruins of Pompeii, Italy, where a Roman fresco depicting an angel and a demon locked in embrace became the song’s starting point. The lyrics follow two dreamers from separate realities who meet at the edge of their daydreams, fall into an obsession, and become trapped in a psychological cage of their own making. Robert describes the result as a “sonic assault of dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago and co-produced by Night Nail in Berlin, with additional vocals and guitar by VV & the Void, the darkwave project of Berlin musician Valentina Veil. Watch the video for ‘Vile Train’ The official video for “Vile Train” is available on YouTube: Night Nail – ‘Vile Train’ (Official Video). ‘Infinite Fountain’ due 6 November “Infinite Fountain” is available for presale on Bandcamp ahead of its 6 November 2026 release through Icy Cold Records. “Vile Train” streams on Spotify. Infinite Fountain by Night Nail About Night Nail Night Nail was founded in Los Angeles in 2013 by Brandon Robert and Justin Deaktiviere. Michael Carpenter Jr. on guitar, David Cluff on bass and Bryan Panzeri on drums joined for the project’s early releases. The project is now based in Berlin, Germany. An early self-titled EP drew press, college radio and blog coverage across the US, Europe, South America and Australia. The band’s debut album, “LA Demons,” was released in July 2018 on Cleopatra Records. Its title draws on Dostoevsky’s novel “Demons.” The sophomore album, “March to Autumn,” followed on 15 October 2020 through Cold Transmission Music. Pete Burns of Kill Shelter co-produced, mixed and mastered the record. Touring and session musicians Valentina Veil, Ilja Gavrilenko and Manuel Wagner contributed additional parts. In September 2023, Night Nail released the single “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher,” the first taste of the album “Fates Explained” on Metropolis Records. The single reached the top five of the Deutsche Alternative Charts. The “Fates Explained” video single followed that November. In January 2024, the band released a video for “Cracks In My Heart,” with Luna De La Torre on vocals, and in July 2024 issued “Early Demons & Demos,” a 10th-anniversary edition of early material. “Vile Train,” released 2 October 2026 through Icy Cold Records, is the first single from “Infinite Fountain,” due 6 November 2026.
items._cn_summary: Night Nail 是一支驻扎柏林的暗潮乐队，2026年10月发行单曲《Vile Train》，作为新专辑《Infinite Fountain》的首支数字单曲，11月通过法国厂牌 Icy Cold Records 发行。歌曲由主创 Brandon Robert 创作，灵感源自庞贝古城的罗马壁画，歌词描写两个梦境中的角色相遇后陷入执念的心理牢笼。作者将作品形容为以扭曲却优美方式呈现的黑暗爱情真相。混音与后期由芝加哥 13 Studio 的 William Faith 完成，柏林音乐人 Valentina Veil 参与客串人声与吉他。乐队前身可追溯至2013年洛杉矶，自首张专辑《LA Demons》起持续与欧洲独立厂牌合作，风格稳固但并未展现突破性的实验倾向。内容以新闻稿形式呈现，缺乏深度乐评视角。

items.body: Einstürzende Neubauten’s debut studio album, “Kollaps,” turns 45 this year. The German industrial band released the record on 5 October 1981 through the Hamburg label ZickZack. It remains the first official full-length release by Blixa Bargeld, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit under the Einstürzende Neubauten name. “Kollaps” runs 38 minutes across eleven tracks, recorded in Berlin in 1981 and produced by the band itself. The album mixes rough punk-derived song structures with noise generated from self-built devices, electronics and metal plates and other found objects, a method that became the band’s signature. The tracklist includes “Tanz Debil,” “Steh auf Berlin,” “Negativ Nein,” “U-Haft Muzak,” “Draußen ist Feindlich,” “Schmerzen Hören (Hören mit Schmerzen),” “Jet’M” (a cover of Serge Gainsbourg’s “Je t’aime… moi non plus”), the title track “Kollaps,” “Sehnsucht,” “Vorm Krieg” and “Hirnsäge.” Later CD reissues appended additional tracks, including a live 1987 recording of “Negativ Nein.” Trouser Press described the record as “one of the most shocking visions ever committed to vinyl.” “Kollaps” is also listed in the reference book “1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.” The album has since been reissued, including a 2002 edition paired with the 1982 dub companion “Stahldubversions.” About Einstürzende Neubauten Einstürzende Neubauten formed in Berlin in 1980 around vocalist and guitarist Blixa Bargeld and percussionist N.U. Unruh. The band’s name translates to “collapsing new buildings,” a reference to construction failures in West Berlin at the time. From the outset, the group built its sound around self-made and adapted instruments, including power tools, scrap metal, oil drums and construction debris, played alongside conventional guitar, bass and vocals. F.M. Einheit joined on percussion before the band’s first LP. The band’s earliest recorded appearance came via the cassette-only “Stahlmusik” in 1980. Einstürzende Neubauten signed to the Hamburg independent label ZickZack, which released “Kollaps” on 5 October 1981, the band’s first official studio album. The record was recorded in Berlin during 1981 and produced by the band itself, with no outside producer credited. Following “Kollaps,” Einstürzende Neubauten continued to record for European independent labels through the 1980s, including “Zeichnungen des Patienten O.T.” (1983) and the compilation “Strategies Against Architecture ’80-’83,” before moving to Some Bizzare/Mute for later releases. Bargeld also worked as a guitarist with Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds from the band’s formation in 1983. Einstürzende Neubauten’s lineup has changed over four decades, with Alexander Hacke and Marc Chung both joining in the years following “Kollaps.” The band added bassist Josefine Lukschy in 2026, alongside confirmed festival dates and studio webcasts. Forty-five years after “Kollaps” introduced the band’s self-made-instrument method on record, Einstürzende Neubauten remains active, with the album standing as the starting point of that catalogue.

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

Rapper R-Shitei and DJ Matsunaga make a compelling double act. R-Shitei packs his verses with quick, tightly controlled syllables, while Matsunaga cuts into the beats with scratches and rhythmic accents. Their sound gives the ear plenty to follow: the pace of the rapping, the shifting percussion and the hooks that emerge from all that activity.

‘Biriken’ opened the set with a bouncing Jersey club rhythm, followed by ‘Yofukashi no Uta’ and the jazzy ‘Daten’. The mood grew darker with ‘doppelgänger’ and ‘Chxxai’, whose pounding beats and electronic textures brought the selection closer to a late-night club set.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Creepy Nuts (@creepynuts_official)

A dedicated DJ routine gave Matsunaga the spotlight midway through. Scratching, quick cuts and beat juggling are central to his performance style, making the decks an instrument with their own rhythmic voice. The placement gave both halves of the partnership their due before the instantly recognisable ‘Bling-Bang-Bang-Born’.

From there, the duo moved through ‘Mirage’, ‘Fright’ and ‘Nidone’, saving ‘Otonoke’ for last. The DAN DA DAN opening theme was a crowd favourite, rounding off their energetic set before The Weeknd took the stage.

items.body:
pami explores why knowing better doesn’t always mean walking away on her latest single, ‘loser’.

Released on 30 September, the Thai singer-songwriter’s track follows someone caught in an on-and-off situationship, choosing an unfulfilling connection over the prospect of being alone. Feelings linger even when commitment remains elusive, leaving its protagonist willing to accept another disappointment just to keep someone close.

Co-written by pami and Jett Blyton, with production by Maribelle, ‘loser’ took shape at a songwriting camp in Australia. Its demo was written and produced in a single day, following a conversation between the songwriters about their own experiences of unhealthy and disappointing relationships.

That shared experience informs the song’s central dilemma: recognising a hurtful pattern can be easier than finding the resolve to leave it. Through its story of teenage romance, ‘loser’ examines the gap between wanting genuine affection and settling for what is available.

Hailing from Phuket, pami works across bedroom pop and indie, pairing personal storytelling with atmospheric melodies. She debuted under Juicey in 2024 and released her first full-length album, puffette, the following year. Her catalogue includes ‘pity dirty’, ‘kiss me blue’, and this year’s ‘cry jar’ and ‘all in’.

items.body:
Charlie Lim is heading back to Manila after seven years, with a new collaboration arriving ahead of his visit.

The Singaporean singer-songwriter will hold an intimate showcase of his latest album, DAYDREAM, at ANALOG MNL, Rockwell Center, Makati, on 11 October. Featuring a vinyl listening session and an exclusive performance, the event will also see him joined by Clara Benin and Young Cocoa.

Fans can sign up for an invitation here.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Charlie Lim 林宇 (@wherewascharlie)

Lim last performed in Manila at Wanderland Music Festival in 2019. This time, he is looking forward to sharing his music in a smaller setting.

“Festivals are always exciting, but there’s something different about being in a smaller room where you can actually sit with the songs and have a proper conversation with people,” he shares. “DAYDREAM is a very personal record, so being able to share it that way feels quite fitting.”

Ahead of the showcase, Lim will release a new version of ‘One Day I’ll Learn’ featuring Young Cocoa at midnight on 7 October. The Filipino rapper contributes an additional verse to the DAYDREAM track, offering his own perspective on regret, self-reflection, and learning from past mistakes.

“What made the collaboration really interesting to me was that Young Cocoa brought a perspective I would not have naturally arrived at on my own,” Lim explains. “His verse really gives the song another voice and another way of looking at that idea.”

Young Cocoa approached the track by listening without reading its lyrics first, allowing his emotional response and personal experiences to guide his writing. Lim’s openness also gave him room to experiment.

“I remember telling him I might get weird with it or experimental, and there was no opposition from his end,” the rapper says. “I relish and thrive when I get to explore all the creative pathways, and having Charlie be encouraging and generally laid-back throughout the process made it easy.”

The pair worked remotely, with Young Cocoa’s melodic choices making a particular impression on Lim.

“I couldn’t stop smiling when he sent over the demo; he really took it to another place, and I am so honoured to have such a talent hop on a song from DAYDREAM.”

Lim will also participate in FILSCAP’s Asia Songwriting Master Camp 2026, joining songwriters from across the region.

items.body:
Echoes of Earth Moves To Nandi Foothills With Thievery Corporation, Yussef Dayes, Lubiana & More For 10th Edition

5 October 2026

Echoes of Earth has just announced the lineup for its 10th edition, which sees the ecologically conscious music festival move to a location in the Nandi Hills outside Bengaluru on December 5-6.

The 2-day festival will see iconic music duo Thievery Corporation make their Asia debut at the festival alongside the likes of prominent British drummer Yussef Dayes and Hamburg techno act MEUTE, who also make their India debut. Meanwhile, a regular to the country, Parra For Cuva, also features on the lineup, while Joris Voorn also returns to India as he makes his festival debut. They will be joined by Thai multidisciplinary artist NOTEP, kora specialist and singer-songwriter Lubiana, as well as Manchester space rock act HENGE.

Among homegrown talent, two techno giants of the country, Arjun Vagale and Anyasa, will do a B2B and so will FILM and Rafiki. Calm Chor will bring his live act, which will feature Elvis Lobo, Life Enjoyers Club and Ranjit Arapurakal. An understated surprise on the lineup will be Sulk Station, the Bangalore duo that remained indie darlings in the former half of the last decade and have laid low since.

Other acts on the lineup include Weval, Sweely, Hearthug, Fish56Octagon, Curtain Blue, Monophonik, When Chai Met Toast, Ulloo, Tamil Jazz Collective, Hashbass, Answer, Alboe, Tristan Bres, Sakré, Syeyl, and Kamari.

For tickets, head here, and follow Echoes of Earth for more updates and full lineup.

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Finnish band Von Hertzen Brothers released their fifth studio album 'Nine Lives' in 2013 throughUniversal, having previously caught the attention of the press with the records 'Love Remains theSame' and 'Stars Aligned'. This quintet plays an interesting crossover of pop, prog, and folk,offering an eclectic yet accessible type of rock music that definitely has commercial potential butdoes not shy away from unconventional arrangements. The album 'Nine Lives' in particular issubjected to a high-energy, buzzing start, in the face of melodic numbers like 'Insomniac' and'Flowers and Rust', while its ending resorts to mellower, more atmospheric tones that are exploredon the longer songs 'World Without' and 'Prospect for Escape'. Certain instrumental sections are waytoo loud in the recording, especially in the faster tracks in the beginning, but I think thisproblem is taken care of in the second half of the recording. The vocals are fine, but some of thelyrics feel corny, while the album itself strikes you as almost too eclectic, which is probably whatVHB had wanted to do, but this aspect of it may disengage some listeners. I think the main issuewith 'Nine Lives' is the fact that there are very few highlights present. The record is quite solidoverall and the variety of styles covered provides for an engaging listen, but the songs featured onit are mostly hit or miss.

items.excerpt: Magic Wands released the single “Guardians” on October 2, 2026 through Metropolis Records. The Los Angeles dream-pop duo of vocalists and guitarists Dexy and Chris Valentine describe the track as a look back at a period that no longer feels real: “This is a song about looking back on a time in your life that doesn’t feel real anymore, even though it really happened.” “Guardians” is the second track lifted from “Sun Kiss,” a new Magic Wands al
items.body: Magic Wands released the single “Guardians” on October 2, 2026 through Metropolis Records. The Los Angeles dream-pop duo of vocalists and guitarists Dexy and Chris Valentine describe the track as a look back at a period that no longer feels real: “This is a song about looking back on a time in your life that doesn’t feel real anymore, even though it really happened.” “Guardians” is the second track lifted from “Sun Kiss,” a new Magic Wands album due in early 2027. It follows “Diamond Rain”, issued in mid-August, which was the first single from the same record. Guardians by Magic Wands “Guardians” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp. Magic Wands’ 2026 singles and EPs “Guardians” and “Diamond Rain” extend a run of releases that started with “Cascades,” the album Magic Wands issued on October 24, 2025. The duo opened 2026 with “Sacred Mirrors,” a January collaboration with Psychedelic Furs guitarist John Ashton. The six-track “Wishing Well” EP followed in April, and Side-Line reviewed it that August. A six-track “Remixes” EP reworking songs from “Cascades” followed in June. Magic Wands remixed Peter Murphy’s “Swoon” in late spring, and Side-Line covered that single when Peter Murphy released “Swoon (Magic Wands Remix)” on May 29, 2026. About Magic Wands Magic Wands formed in Nashville, Tennessee, in the summer of 2008 around vocalists and guitarists Dexy Valentine and Chris Valentine, who began writing together after Dexy moved from Los Angeles to Nashville. The duo later relocated to Los Angeles, where they are now based. Their sound blends dream-pop with shoegaze, post-punk and goth textures, carried by layered guitars, droning synths and Dexy’s vocals. The band debuted with the album “Aloha Moon” (Bright Antenna, 2012), preceded by the EP “Magic Love & Dreams” (2009). “Jupiter” followed on Cleopatra Records in 2016, and “Abrakadabra” on Etxe Records & Productions / Casa del Puente Discos in 2018. Magic Wands self-released “Illuminate” in 2020, then signed to Metropolis Records for “Switch,” released May 12, 2023. Side-Line reviewed “Switch” that September, having already covered the duo’s single “Fortune” in April 2022, the single “Time” that May, and the remix album and tour announced that August. Magic Wands’ sixth album, “Cascades,” arrived in October 2025 and set off the run of singles, remixes and EPs that continued through 2026. “Guardians” now carries that chronology into “Sun Kiss,” the duo’s next album, scheduled for early 2027.
